items.title: Insurance, gold and fuel no longer count for fee waiver
items.summary: Spends on insurance, gold and fuel are now ignored when Axis checks whether you hit the target to get your annual fee waived, so those purchases no longer help you dodge the fee. Rent, wallet, utility, government, EMI and cash spends were already excluded.

items.title: 1% fee on fees paid via education apps
items.summary: Paying college or school fees through third-party apps now costs 1% plus GST on every transaction, so ₹1,00,000 of fees costs ₹1,000 plus tax. Paying the institution directly on its own website or POS machine avoids the fee.

items.title: 1% fee on fuel spends above ₹50,000 a month
items.summary: If your petrol/diesel spends on the card cross ₹50,000 in one statement cycle, a 1% fee plus GST applies on the amount. That's ₹500 plus tax on ₹50,000 of fuel.

items.title: 1% fee on gaming spends above ₹10,000 a month
items.summary: Spending on online skill-based gaming platforms now attracts 1% plus GST once it crosses ₹10,000 in a statement cycle. Spend ₹12,000 and you pay ₹120 plus tax.

items.title: 1% fee on utility bills above ₹25,000 a month
items.summary: Electricity, water and similar utility bills paid with the card attract 1% plus GST once they total ₹25,000 in a statement cycle. On ₹25,000 of bills that's ₹250 plus tax.

items.title: 1% fee on wallet loads above ₹10,000 a month
items.summary: Loading Paytm/PhonePe-type wallets with your Axis card now costs 1% plus GST once your wallet loads cross ₹10,000 in a statement cycle. Load ₹12,000 and you pay ₹120 plus tax.

items.title: Interest on unpaid dues is 3.75% a month
items.summary: If you pay less than the total amount due, interest runs at 3.75% per month (55.55% a year) on most Axis cards. Reserve, Magnus and Olympus are charged 3.0% per month and Burgundy Private 1.5% per month.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad now costs 1.5%, not 1%
items.summary: When you let an overseas merchant or website charge you in INR instead of the local currency, Axis now takes 1.5% plus GST instead of 1%. On a ₹50,000 booking that's ₹750 plus tax instead of ₹500.

items.title: Rent payment fee no longer capped at ₹1,500
items.summary: The 1% fee on rent paid with an Axis card used to stop at ₹1,500 per transaction; the cap is gone, so a ₹3 lakh rent payment now costs ₹3,000 plus GST instead of ₹1,500.

items.title: No interest on over-limit loan EMIs from May 2026
items.summary: From 30 May 2026, if you are revolving your balance, Axis will not charge interest on EMIs of an Over-the-Limit Instant Loan, unlike all other billed EMIs. That saves interest for anyone carrying such a loan.

items.title: Magnus fee waived for new Burgundy Salary accounts
items.summary: Customers with a Burgundy Salary Account opened on or after 1 July 2026 pay no joining or annual fee on Magnus, instead of ₹12,500. The waiver lasts only while you keep the required Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Extra ₹100 if you miss minimum due twice
items.summary: Miss your minimum amount due for two statement cycles in a row and Axis adds ₹100 on top of the normal late payment fee, and keeps charging it every cycle until you clear the minimum due.

items.title: Infinia now needs ₹18L spend or ₹50L balance
items.summary: From 1 April 2026, you keep your Infinia card only if you spend ₹18 lakh a year on it or hold ₹50 lakh average across your HDFC accounts. Miss both and the bank can move you off the Infinia programme.

items.title: 1.75% markup on rupee spends at foreign merchants
items.summary: From 15 May 2026, paying in rupees at an overseas location or at an India-based merchant registered abroad costs you an extra 1.75% markup. This hits things like foreign websites that bill you in INR.

items.title: Late fees now apply to Insta Jumbo Loan EMIs
items.summary: From 20 June 2026, missing or part-paying an Insta Jumbo Loan EMI attracts a late fee of ₹100 to ₹1,300 plus GST, based on how much you owe. Nothing is charged if the outstanding is ₹100 or less.

items.title: Government payments now treated as utility spends
items.summary: Government transactions are clubbed with utility payments, so they follow your card's utility reward rules instead of being counted separately. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: Zero reward points on rent and wallet top-ups
items.summary: Rent payments and loading money into e-wallets earn you no reward points at all, so those big-ticket spends now give you nothing back. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is the only exception.

items.title: Free airport lounge needs ₹75,000 spend per quarter
items.summary: Since 1 January 2025, domestic lounge visits are only free if you spent ₹75,000 on the card in the previous quarter, and that unlocks access for the next quarter. Rent, government, education and EMI payments don't count towards the ₹75,000.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad now costs up to 3.5% extra
items.summary: From 15 January 2026, ICICI revises the Dynamic Currency Conversion fee charged when you pay in Indian rupees at an overseas shop or at an India-based merchant registered abroad — 3.50% on most cards, 2.00% on Emeralde cards, 1.99% on Amazon Pay, 1.49% on Times Black and 0.99% on the MakeMyTrip Travel card. Always choose to pay in the local currency instead to dodge this fee.

items.title: BookMyShow perk needs ₹25,000 spend every quarter
items.summary: From 1 April 2026, your BookMyShow movie benefit is no longer automatic — you must spend at least ₹25,000 on the card in the previous quarter to unlock it for the next quarter. Spend less and you lose the ticket offer for those three months.

items.title: Cardless ATM cash withdrawal shuts down Feb 21
items.summary: You can no longer pull cash from RBL or non-RBL ATMs without your card after 21 February 2026, so carry your debit card. The Rs. 20 per transaction fee for this service goes away with it, and paid fees for expired or cancelled transactions are not refunded.

items.title: Cap on points you can use as statement credit
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can convert only 60,000 reward points a month into statement credit, so big balances take longer to use up. Air India SBI Signature and both PhonePe cards are exempt.

items.title: Cashback SBI Card benefits are being changed
items.summary: SBI says the benefits on the CASHBACK SBI Credit Card change from 1 April 2026, but the notice itself does not print the old and new values. Check the linked details before relying on your cashback.

items.title: Statement credit only in blocks of 4,000 points
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can redeem points for statement credit only in multiples of 4,000, so leftover points below that stay stuck. PhonePe Purple and Select Black cards are exempt.

items.title: BPCL card fee waiver needs double the spending
items.summary: You now have to spend ₹1 lakh a year instead of ₹50,000 to get the ₹499 annual fee refunded on your BPCL SBI Card. Spend less and you simply pay the fee.

items.title: Small late payments now cost you a fee
items.summary: From 1 May 2026, missing a payment on a bill as small as ₹101 will cost you ₹100, and dues between ₹500 and ₹1,000 jump from ₹400 to ₹500. Earlier anything under ₹500 was free.

items.title: No points on tolls, jewellery, fees on PhonePe cards
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your PhonePe SBI cards stop earning points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, school and college fees, and on utilities, insurance or UPI paid outside the PhonePe app. Those spends will now earn you nothing.

items.title: PhonePe Purple card reward caps cut
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your monthly reward cap on PhonePe spends drops from 1,000 points to 750 (only 250 for insurance), and online spends drop from 1,000 to 750 points. That means fewer points for the same spending.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black reward caps halved online
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 the monthly cap on online spends falls from 2,000 points to 1,000, and PhonePe spends from 2,000 to 1,500 points (just 500 for insurance). Heavy users will hit the ceiling much sooner.

items.title: New INR 550 charge for spending over your limit
items.summary: From 1 June 2026 YES Bank will let some transactions go through above your credit limit, but each such transaction costs INR 550 plus GST. If you don't want the charge, keep spends inside your limit.

items.title: POP-Club fuel waiver capped at INR 100 a month
items.summary: From 1 June 2026 the POP-Club card's 1% fuel surcharge waiver only applies to fuel bills between INR 1,000 and INR 3,500, and the monthly waiver is capped at INR 100 instead of INR 300. Small or large fill-ups get nothing back.

items.title: Cash withdrawal fee jumps to min INR 650
items.summary: Taking cash out on your YES Bank credit card will cost you at least INR 650 instead of INR 500 from 15 June 2026 (2.5% if higher). Interest also starts from day one on cash withdrawals.

items.title: Elite+, Essence, Prosperity Business forex now 3.00%
items.summary: Overseas and foreign-currency spends on these cards cost 3.00% from 15 June 2026, up from 2.75% (Elite+, YES Essence) and 2.50% (YES Prosperity Business). Budget an extra INR 250-500 per INR 1 lakh spent abroad.

items.title: Failed auto-debit now costs more, cap raised to 5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces after 15 June 2026, the penalty rises to 2.5% or INR 500 (whichever is higher) from 2% or INR 450, and the monthly ceiling on these charges jumps from INR 1,500 to INR 5,000. Multiple bounces can now cost you far more in a single statement.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver limits redrawn per card
items.summary: From 15 June 2026 the fuel bill sizes that qualify for the 1% surcharge waiver change by card: INR 500-5,000 for premium cards, INR 500-4,000 for Elite+/Reserv/Essence/Niyo, and INR 500-3,000 for ACE, Select, Wellness, BYOC and similar. Fill-ups below INR 500 no longer get the waiver on most cards.

items.title: New INR 250 fee for paying card bill by cheque
items.summary: From 15 June 2026, paying your card bill by cheque at a YES Bank branch costs INR 250 plus GST if the payment is INR 1,000 or more. Digital payment modes avoid this fee.

items.title: Paying your card bill in cash now costs INR 500
items.summary: Depositing cash at a YES Bank branch to pay your card bill of INR 1,000 or more will cost INR 500 plus GST from 15 June 2026, up from INR 100. Pay online instead to avoid it.

items.title: Prosperity and co-brand cards forex up to 3.50%
items.summary: Foreign spends on these cards cost 3.50% from 15 June 2026, up from 3.40%. Small rise, but it applies to every international transaction.

items.title: Replacing a lost card now costs INR 199
items.summary: If your plastic card is lost, stolen or damaged, a replacement costs INR 199 from 15 June 2026 instead of INR 100. BYOC Eco-friendly and Metal card fees stay the same.

items.title: Reserv and YES First forex markup up to 2.00%
items.summary: Foreign currency spends on these cards will cost 2.00% instead of 1.75% from 15 June 2026. That's INR 250 more on every INR 1 lakh spent overseas.

items.title: Select and ACE forex markup rises to 3.50%
items.summary: Spending abroad or on foreign websites with these cards costs 3.50% of the amount from 15 June 2026, up from 2.75% — about INR 750 extra on a INR 1 lakh foreign spend. Plus GST on top.

items.title: No interest on over-limit loan EMIs from May 2026
items.summary: From 30 May 2026, if you revolve your balance you will not be charged interest on EMIs of an Over-the-Limit Instant Loan on your card. Interest still applies on all your other spends and EMIs.

items.title: Horizon card free with new Burgundy Savings A/c
items.summary: The ₹3,000 joining and annual fee on the Horizon card is nil if you open a Burgundy Savings Account on or after 1 July 2026. The waiver depends on you keeping that Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Magnus fee waived for new Burgundy Salary users
items.summary: You save the ₹12,500 joining and annual fee on the Magnus card if you open a Burgundy Salary Account on or after 1 July 2026. Everyone else keeps paying ₹12,500.

items.title: Paying abroad in rupees now costs 1.5%, not 1%
items.summary: If you let an overseas shop or website bill you in Indian rupees, Axis now charges 1.5% plus GST on that amount instead of 1%. Burgundy Private, Olympus and Primus cards pay nothing.

items.title: Rent fee of 1% no longer capped at ₹1,500
items.summary: Paying rent on your Axis card now costs a flat 1% plus GST on every transaction with no upper limit, so big rent payments cost more than before. Olympus and Primus cards pay no rent fee.

items.title: Infinia now needs ₹18L spend a year to keep
items.summary: From 1 April 2026, HDFC will only let you keep your Infinia card if you spend ₹18 lakh in a financial year (primary + add-ons) or hold ₹50 lakh in average bank balances. Fall short and the bank can move you to a different card.

items.title: New 1.75% markup on rupee spends abroad
items.summary: From 15 May 2026, paying in rupees at an overseas merchant or an India-based merchant registered abroad will cost you an extra 1.75% of the transaction. This applies even though you never touched foreign currency.

items.title: Late fee on Insta Jumbo loan EMIs from June 2026
items.summary: If you miss or partly pay an Insta Jumbo loan EMI from 20 June 2026, a late fee plus GST kicks in, ranging from ₹100 on small dues to ₹1,300 when you owe over ₹50,000. Nothing is charged if the outstanding is ₹100 or less.

items.title: Government payments now counted as utility spends
items.summary: Government payments are treated as utility transactions, so they earn only the (usually capped) utility reward rate on your card. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: No reward points on rent or wallet top-ups
items.summary: Rent payments and loading money into e-wallets earn you zero reward points, so those spends are effectively unrewarded. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: Free airport lounge needs ₹75,000 spend a quarter
items.summary: Complimentary domestic lounge visits are earned, not given: you must spend ₹75,000 in the previous quarter to get access in the next quarter. Rent, government, education and EMI payments, fees and interest do not count towards that ₹75,000.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad gets a new fee from 15 Jan 2026
items.summary: From 15 January 2026 ICICI Bank charges a revised Dynamic Currency Conversion fee every time you let an overseas machine (or a foreign-registered merchant in India) bill you in rupees — 3.50% on most cards, 2.00% on Emeralde cards, 1.99% on Amazon Pay, 1.49% on Times Black and 0.99% on the MakeMyTrip Travel card. Always choose to pay in the local currency to avoid it.

items.title: Free movie benefit now needs ₹25,000 spend a quarter
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 your BookMyShow offer is no longer automatic — you must spend ₹25,000 in the previous quarter to unlock it for the next quarter. Spend less and you get no movie benefit that quarter.

items.title: Cardless ATM cash withdrawal being scrapped
items.summary: From 21 February 2026 you can no longer pull cash from RBL or other ATMs using IMT cardless withdrawal, so you'll need your debit card. The Rs. 20 per transaction fee for the service goes away along with the service itself.

items.title: CASHBACK SBI Card benefits are being changed
items.summary: SBI Card says the benefits on the CASHBACK SBI Credit Card change from 1 April 2026, so what you earn may differ. The notice does not print the old and new values on this page.

items.title: Monthly limit on cashing in reward points
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can convert only 60,000 reward points a month into statement credit, so large point balances take longer to use up. Air India SBI Signature and both PhonePe SBI cards are not affected.

items.title: Points redeemed only in blocks of 4,000
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 statement-credit redemptions must be in multiples of 4,000 points, so leftover points below that stay stuck on your account. The two PhonePe SBI cards are excluded from this rule.

items.title: BPCL card: spend 1 lakh to dodge Rs.499 fee
items.summary: From 1 May 2026 you must spend Rs.1 lakh a year on your BPCL SBI Card to get the Rs.499 annual fee refunded, double the earlier Rs.50,000. Spend less and you simply pay the fee.

items.title: Late payment now costs you on small bills too
items.summary: From 1 May 2026, missing a payment on a bill as small as Rs.100 will cost you Rs.100, where earlier anything up to Rs.500 was free. The Rs.500–Rs.1,000 slab also rises from Rs.400 to Rs.500.

items.title: No points on tolls, jewellery, fees on PhonePe cards
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your PhonePe SBI cards stop earning any reward points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, school and college fees, and on utility, insurance or UPI payments made outside the PhonePe app. These everyday spends will now earn you zero.

items.title: PhonePe Purple card: monthly reward cap cut
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 you can earn far fewer points each month on your PhonePe SBI Card PURPLE — PhonePe spends drop from 1,000 points to 750 (only 250 on insurance), and other online spends drop from 1,000 to 750. Spend beyond that and you get nothing extra.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black: reward caps halved
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your PhonePe SBI Card SELECT BLACK earns fewer points monthly — PhonePe spends fall from 2,000 points to 1,500 (500 on insurance), and online spends fall from 2,000 to 1,000. Anything above the cap earns you nothing.

items.title: Overspending your limit will cost INR 550
items.summary: YES BANK is bringing back the overlimit facility from 1 June 2026, letting transactions go through above your credit limit — but each one costs INR 550 plus GST. If you would rather not pay this, keep your spending inside your limit.

items.title: POP-Club fuel waiver limited to INR 1,000-3,500 spends
items.summary: From 1 June 2026, POP-Club cardholders only get the 1% fuel surcharge waiver on fills between INR 1,000 and INR 3,500, capped at INR 100 per statement cycle. Fills below INR 1,000 or above INR 3,500 get no waiver.

items.title: Cash withdrawal on your card gets costlier
items.summary: Taking cash out on your YES BANK credit card will cost you at least INR 650 instead of INR 500 from 15 June 2026. The 2.5% rate stays the same, but the minimum floor fee goes up.

items.title: Failed auto-debit fee jumps, cap rises to INR 5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces, the fee rises from 2% (min INR 450) to 2.5% (min INR 500) from 15 June 2026. Worse, the monthly cap on these charges goes from INR 1,500 to INR 5,000 per statement.

items.title: Forex markup rises on most YES BANK cards
items.summary: Spending abroad or on foreign websites gets more expensive from 15 June 2026 on several cards — for example Reserv and YES First Preferred go from 1.75% to 2%, Elite+ from 2.75% to 3%, and Select/Ace from 2.75% to 3.5%. YES Private, Marquee, FREO and BYOC rates stay unchanged.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver window changes on many cards
items.summary: From 15 June 2026 the transaction amounts that qualify for the 1% fuel surcharge waiver change by card — most cards move from INR 400–5,000 to bands like INR 500–5,000, INR 500–4,000 or INR 500–3,000, so small fill-ups under INR 500 no longer qualify. Paisabazaar Paisasave holders move from INR 500–3,000 to INR 500–3,000 range under the new table.

items.title: New INR 250 fee for paying by cheque
items.summary: From 15 June 2026, paying your card bill by cheque at a branch costs INR 250 plus GST if the amount is INR 1,000 or more. There was no such fee before.

items.title: Paying your card bill in cash now costs INR 500
items.summary: Depositing cash at a YES BANK branch to pay your card bill of INR 1,000 or more will cost INR 500 plus GST from 15 June 2026, up from INR 100. Pay online instead and you avoid this entirely.

items.title: Replacing a lost card now costs INR 199
items.summary: If your plastic card is lost, stolen or damaged, the replacement fee doubles from INR 100 to INR 199 from 15 June 2026. Metal and eco-friendly BYOC cards keep their existing fees.
